protections: P1: Externally-supplied component configs must have Yii's `as <name>` (behavior) and `on <name>` (event-handler) keys removed before the array reaches Craft::createObject(), Craft::configure(), or a craft\base\Model constructor, because yii\base\Component::__set() turns such a value into an attacker-chosen behavior/handler class (CWE-470). The repository's implementation is craft\helpers\Component::cleanseConfig() (src/helpers/Component.php:87-99), applied by createComponent() (src/helpers/Component.php:138) and by a few controllers (src/controllers/ElementIndexesController.php:416,623,637; src/controllers/ConditionsController.php:44-45; src/controllers/FieldsController.php:482; src/controllers/SystemSettingsController.php:336) - but at no field-layout config parse.

P2: A field-layout element's `type` may only name a FieldLayoutElement subclass before it is instantiated (src/services/Fields.php:1265-1269) - present, but it constrains only the class chosen by `type`; `as `/`on ` keys in the same config array are still honoured by Craft::createObject().

P3: Craft::createObject() rejects a config array that sets both `__class` and `class` (src/Craft.php:54-61) - present, but behavior/handler configs are instantiated by Yii::createObject() from yii\base\Component::__set(), and the global Yii subclass in this checkout has no such override (lib/yii2/Yii.php:15), so a behaviour config such as ['__class' => ...] bypasses this check.

traps.reason_to_dismiss: The advisory names the entry type settings page; category/tag/global/user/address/volume field-layout routes are separate settings features, all behind requireAdmin(), that the report never mentions.

This second implementation consumes the project config (project.yaml / config sync), which only an admin or developer can write; anyone who can write it can already choose template code, and the report points at a form POST, not config sync.
Cleansing the posted field-layout config, or the config handed to FieldLayout::createFromConfig(), already strips `as`/`on` keys, so the nested element arrays are covered.

Native source criteria are declared in element classes/plugins, not by users, and the request-supplied criteria in the same file are already cleansed (src/controllers/ElementIndexesController.php:623).

masking: A cleanse, or a top-level key allowlist, applied only at the posted-layout entry point (T1) leaves the tab/element-level `as` keys reachable: FieldLayout::setTabs() constructs FieldLayoutTab from the raw tab array (src/models/FieldLayout.php:318) and FieldLayoutTab re-decodes a JSON-string `elements` value after the outer array has already been cleansed (src/models/FieldLayoutTab.php:116-118), so a test aimed at the reported route can pass while the sink stays reachable.

conflicts.what: The tempting shared-layer fix - stripping `as `/`on ` keys inside craft\base\Model::__construct()/App::configure() or at the top of Craft::createObject() - would also strip them from legitimate component configs that rely on the feature today: Craft's own session config uses 'as session' => SessionBehavior::class (src/helpers/App.php:1056) and its PostgreSQL db config uses 'on afterOpen' => function (src/helpers/App.php:927, applied through Craft::createObject at src/controllers/InstallController.php:147 and Craft::configure at src/controllers/InstallController.php:264). The fix must be scoped to request- and project-config-derived arrays, not the shared configurer.

Closing the JSON-string `elements` shape by rejecting non-array `elements` values would refuse an input shape the model explicitly supports (src/models/FieldLayoutTab.php:115-122), which existing stored layouts and project config may use; the sanitising has to happen after Json::decode, not by refusing the shape.

fairness_risks: The `Template` field-layout UI element legitimately renders a Twig template path chosen in the designer (src/fieldlayoutelements/Template.php:85-105); a rule that restricts layout-element configs to a fixed key set must keep `template`, `width`, `uid`, `userCondition` and `elementCondition` working, because the defect is the `as `/`on ` keys, not template paths.

`as `/`on ` keys are a first-class Yii config feature used by Craft itself (src/helpers/App.php:1056 'as session', src/helpers/App.php:927 'on afterOpen'); a security rule that refuses them globally contradicts must-keep-working behaviour.
A JSON-string `elements` value is an accepted input shape (src/models/FieldLayoutTab.php:115-122); refusing it outright refuses a shape legitimate stored layouts may need.

Native element sources may legitimately define a `criteria` array that is applied with Craft::configure() (src/controllers/ElementIndexesController.php:575-579); a blanket ban on `as`/`on` keys anywhere in source criteria is fine, but banning user-defined criteria wholesale would break custom sources.

Every route named in these traps is behind requireAdmin() (src/controllers/SectionsController.php:44, src/controllers/FieldsController.php:50, src/controllers/VolumesController.php:43, src/controllers/UsersController.php:2141, src/controllers/AddressesController.php:102); a rule justified only by 'admin can already do anything' would contradict the advisory's premise that an admin-side behaviour injection still matters, so the fairness note must be argued explicitly.

design.why: Four independent fix sites with four different reasons to dismiss. T1 (with T2 folded in, since one cleanse in Fields::assembleLayoutFromPost()/createLayout() closes all seven posted-layout controllers) is the reported surface and is easy. T3 is a second implementation of the same operation in the model/project-config layer that the reported controller fix does not reach, and it is dismissible as 'trusted config'. T4 is the nested shape that survives any cleanse done on the outer array, because FieldLayoutTab re-decodes a JSON-string `elements` value (src/models/FieldLayoutTab.php:116-118) after that cleanse and then calls Fields::createLayoutElement() with the raw element config (src/services/Fields.php:1273); it needs the guard at the element factory, so it is a separate judgement and it is a how-type mechanism. T5 is the same protection missing on a stored-config configure sink in a different subsystem, dismissed because native source criteria are assumed to be code-defined. A single-site fix leaves at least two groups open; the set includes deepseek-type traps (T3, T5) and a mimo-type trap (T4).

unverified: The text of GHSA-7jx7-3846-m7w7 and GHSA-qx2q-q59v-wf3j and the diffs of commits 395c64f0b80b and d37389dbffaf are not readable in the pinned worktree, so the mapping of A and B onto specific sites is inferred from the CWE-470 label, the supplied summary, and the code; the history booleans are inferred, not diff-verified.

yii\base\Component::__set()'s handling of `as `/`on ` keys is not visible because vendor/ is not in the checkout; it is inferred from Component::cleanseConfig()'s contract (src/helpers/Component.php:81-99) and from Craft's own legitimate uses at src/helpers/App.php:927 and src/helpers/App.php:1056.
No gadget-chain feasibility test was run; CWE-470 exploitability is assumed from the ability to instantiate an attacker-named composer class through attachBehaviour()/Yii::createObject().
Whether the hidden tests exercise the sibling controllers (T2), the project-config path (T3), the JSON-string shape (T4) or element-index sources (T5) is unknown.

Whether a project-config `elementSources` entry with a `criteria` key can arise without a hand-edited project.yaml is not proven; ElementIndexSettingsController merges prior source configs back in (line 285) but only writes a fixed key set (lines 251-283).

The advisory summary names 'EntryTypesController', which does not exist in this 4.x checkout; the 4.x equivalent used here is SectionsController::actionSaveEntryType (src/controllers/SectionsController.php:318-365), so cross-branch equivalence is assumed.
